title.zh: 同一句玩笑，可以从不同角度看
title.en: One joke can have several angles

paragraphs.zh: 虚构例子：两个人带了四把伞，你平静地说“今天的防雨部门人员很充足”。认真口吻形成反差，体现冷面；把雨伞编成部门，又带一点荒诞。如果围绕大家刚刚带伞的经历，也可能有共同趣味。六份读法比较的是不同观察角度，不要求把一句话只归到一类。
paragraphs.en: In a fictional outing, two people bring four umbrellas. A level remark about the generously staffed rain-prevention department uses deadpan contrast and an absurd invented department. Referring to the group’s shared umbrella incident can add shared humor too. These guides offer different observation angles rather than require one category for a line.

title.zh: 没有被接住时，怎样结束也算观察
title.en: How a missed line ends is worth noticing

paragraphs.zh: 接着上面的低调玩笑尝试，回看听众是否知道哪部分是认真信息，哪部分在开玩笑。若需要解释，一句“我是说伞比人还多”就可以，然后回到原话题。不需要追问“你怎么不笑”，也不把一次解释当作冷面表达失败；问卷没有测笑点的正确答案。
paragraphs.en: After the understated remark above, consider whether the audience could separate practical information from play. A brief explanation that there are more umbrellas than people may be enough before returning to the topic. No request for a laugh is needed. Explaining once is not a failed deadpan score; this reflection has no correct joke response.

title.zh: 分享口吻偏好，而非冷漠标签
title.en: Share a delivery preference without a coldness label

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“你更喜欢听出语气反差，还是希望玩笑有明显提示？在文字里呢？”可以用一个无关真人的小例子，不公布均分。喜欢冷面不代表平时冷漠，不喜欢也不说明缺少幽默感；对方可以只讨论自己想谈的表达方式。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “Do you enjoy a matter-of-fact contrast, or prefer an obvious signal that something is a joke? What about messages?” Use an impersonal example without publishing means. Enjoying deadpan establishes no coldness, and disliking it no lack of humor. Someone may choose which delivery preferences to discuss.

title.zh: 先看字词，再看口吻或情节
title.en: Look at wording before delivery or plot

paragraphs.zh: 中文虚构例子：给一把找回来的汤匙写“匙别三日”，笑点来自改动熟悉表达的字；英语可以另写一只汤匙说自己想“stir things up”，利用搅拌与制造动静的两种读法。两句是各自语言里的编辑举例，不互相考翻译。它们也可以被冷面地说出，或发展成荒诞故事。
paragraphs.en: For an original Chinese example, a rediscovered spoon receives a familiar phrase rewritten with the character for spoon. An independent English example gives a spoon an ambition to “stir things up,” playing on stirring and creating commotion. These are language-specific illustrations, not translation questions. Either can use deadpan delivery or become an absurd story.

title.zh: 回看让双关成立的共同材料
title.en: Review what made the wordplay accessible

paragraphs.zh: 接着上面的语言观察尝试，看看玩笑需要知道哪个词义、读音或固定说法。若对方不熟悉，解释材料就好，不替对方补一个“听不懂”的能力评价。也允许你只欣赏别人讲的双关而不主动造梗；本版题目问的是使用频率，不能由欣赏补出次数。
paragraphs.en: After the language observation above, identify the meaning, sound or familiar expression needed for the joke. If it is unfamiliar, explain the material without judging the listener’s ability. You may enjoy other people’s puns without making them. These items ask about use; appreciation cannot supply an unreported frequency.

title.zh: 邀请一个词的不同读法
title.en: Invite another reading of a word

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“最近有没有一个词，让你想到两种意思？说不出来也可以，听例子就好。”分享自己愿意讲的词，不拿朋友的姓名、口音或语言错误当素材。公开读法不附个人均分，也不代表词汇量、智力或谁更会写作。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “Has a word recently suggested two meanings to you? You can just listen to an example if none comes to mind.” Share a word you choose without making a friend’s name, accent or language error the material. This public reading carries no means or judgment of vocabulary, intelligence or writing skill.

title.zh: 虚构规则与字词游戏，区别在哪里
title.en: How do imaginary rules differ from wordplay?

paragraphs.zh: 虚构例子：你说厨房的汤匙正在竞选“搅拌事务部长”，笑点来自把物品放进不可能的职务，不一定依赖双关。若再用“匙别三日”这样的改字，则加入文字巧思；若平静宣布，则加入冷面。把机制分开看，更容易讨论自己实际用了什么，而不是争论只能属于哪一种幽默。
paragraphs.en: In a fictional kitchen, a spoon campaigns to become minister for stirring. The humor assigns an object an impossible office without necessarily using a pun. Adding “stir things up” introduces wordplay, while announcing it matter-of-factly adds deadpan. Separate mechanisms to discuss what occurred rather than argue for one exclusive humor category.

title.zh: 故事停在哪里，现实信息还清楚吗
title.en: Where did the story stop, and was reality still clear?

paragraphs.zh: 接着上面的物品想象尝试，回看双方是否共享“这是假想”的前提，什么时候想停止，以及原本的小事有没有处理清楚。有人不想继续编，可以自然结束，不要求解释品味。没有完整故事也可以获得观察；这不是创造力训练的效果评估，更不需要提高频率。
paragraphs.en: After the object-imagination trial above, review the shared fictional premise, when each person wanted to stop, and whether the practical matter stayed clear. End naturally if someone does not want to continue. An incomplete story can still offer an observation. This is no evaluation of creativity training and requires no increased frequency.

title.zh: 分享一个物品的虚构职位

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“如果这把汤匙有一个完全不可能的职位，你想叫它什么？也可以不接故事。”材料可以只是一件普通物品，不用朋友的私事或真实人物的传闻。分享通用读法不公布均分，也不从愿不愿意玩这个想象推断创造力或心理状态。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If this spoon had a completely impossible job, what would you call it? You can also leave the story there.” Use an ordinary object without private experiences or rumours about real people. Sharing this general reading supplies neither means nor an inference about creativity or mental state from participation.

title.zh: 共同背景与表达机制可以同时存在
title.en: Shared context can coexist with a joke’s mechanism

paragraphs.zh: 虚构例子：几个人一起摆桌时，总找不到同一把汤匙。后来称它为“本场最忙的嘉宾”，可以基于大家都知道的小插曲形成共同趣味，也带一点拟人化的荒诞。新来的人不知道前情时，补一句发生了什么，比要求对方熟悉旧梗更清楚。有人只想继续摆桌也可以。
paragraphs.en: In a fictional table-setting, a group keeps losing the same spoon. Calling it the busiest guest can use the shared incident and an absurd personification together. Give a newcomer a brief account instead of expecting familiarity with the old reference. Someone may simply want to continue setting the table.

title.zh: 回看谁有前情，谁想继续
title.en: Review access to the context and interest in continuing

paragraphs.zh: 接着上面的补充前情尝试，回看后来加入的人能否理解材料、故事里的人是否愿意被提及。不要把没有笑声当作必须继续暖场的信号；也许此刻只需把事情做好。可以下次换一个公共的小细节，或不讲。观察参与条件，不把均分当作团队凝聚力或社交能力。
paragraphs.en: After adding context in the trial above, check access for a later arrival and willingness from anyone mentioned. No laughter is not a command to keep lightening the mood; the practical task may matter now. Another shared detail or no joke may fit next time. Observe participation conditions without treating a mean as cohesion or social skill.

title.zh: 邀请一个大家愿意重讲的小插曲
title.en: Invite a small shared incident people want to retell

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“我们有没有一件可以公开重讲的小乌龙？哪段前情需要先解释？”涉及别人时先询问，也允许不讲。分享可以是共同回忆，不必公布均分、比较谁最暖场，或把安静的朋友说成不合群；公开说明只提供通用观察角度。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “Is there a small shared mix-up we would be happy to retell, and what background would it need?” Check with anyone involved and leave room not to tell it. Share a memory without means, a competition for mood-maker status or an exclusion label for a quiet friend. This public guide offers general observation angles.

title.zh: 关于自己的小事，也能用几种机制
title.en: A personal mishap can use several mechanisms

paragraphs.zh: 虚构例子：摆桌时你把汤匙放进笔筒，后来打趣“今天文具部临时借调了餐具”。话题落在自己的一次小混淆，是自嘲；虚构部门又带荒诞，也可以用冷面语气。它没有说你什么都做不好，更不表示愿意让别人一直重复这件事。
paragraphs.en: In a fictional table-setting, you put a spoon in a pen holder and later joke that the stationery department borrowed the cutlery. A minor mix-up of your own supplies self-deprecation; the invented department adds absurdity, perhaps with deadpan delivery. The line makes no global claim of incompetence or permission for repeated jokes about you.

title.zh: 讲过之后，边界仍可以改变
title.en: Boundaries can change after telling a story

paragraphs.zh: 接着上面的个人小插曲尝试，回看你愿意公开到哪里，别人是否开始把一次失误扩大成对你的评价。可以说“这段就讲到这里”，也可以另说实际需要。对方能否停止要看真实回应；自报频率没有测你有多自信，也不能要求你用玩笑接受贬低。
paragraphs.en: After the personal-anecdote trial above, consider the scope you wanted to share and whether one mistake became a judgment of you. You can end the story or state a practical need directly. Whether others stop depends on their actual response. Reported frequency measures no confidence and requires no acceptance of put-downs through humor.

title.zh: 只分享自己愿意讲的一小段
title.en: Share only the small part you choose

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“我愿意讲一个自己的小乌龙，但不想把它变成长期外号。你也可以只听，不必接梗。”无需公布均分，也不从朋友是否自嘲判断谦逊、自卑或心理健康。分享通用读法不等于把个人经历变成可任意传播的素材。
paragraphs.en: Try: “I am happy telling a small mix-up of mine, but would not like it to become a lasting nickname. You can just listen without adding a joke.” No means are needed, and self-deprecation establishes neither humility, low self-esteem nor mental health. Sharing this public guide does not make personal experiences freely reusable.

title.zh: 来回应答，不等于可以调侃一切
title.en: A back-and-forth permits no unlimited teasing

paragraphs.zh: 虚构例子：朋友说带了三份野餐清单，你问“清单管理员也有清单吗？”这是接着前一句细节打趣，也可以加入荒诞内容。如果对方想认真确认物品，就回到实际清单。是不是双方愿意的机锋，要看当下回应，不能由你觉得轻松、彼此熟悉或均分较高来保证。
paragraphs.en: In a fictional picnic plan, a friend mentions three lists and you ask whether the list administrator has a list too. The reply teases a preceding detail and may add absurdity. Return to the practical list if that is what they want to discuss. Familiarity, your light intention or a higher mean cannot establish that the exchange is welcome.

title.zh: 停下之后，不必赢最后一句
title.en: Stopping needs no winning final line

paragraphs.zh: 接着上面的自然玩笑观察，回看对方能否换话题、拒绝或不接。如果出现不舒服，可以停止并回应具体影响，不加一句“你太认真了”继续打趣。也可以选择下次换成不针对个人的想象。目标是了解这次互动，不是证明谁反应快、谁善意或谁更经得起玩笑。
paragraphs.en: After observing the playful exchange above, review room to change the topic, decline or leave a line unanswered. If discomfort appears, stop and address the specific effect without another tease about taking things seriously. An impersonal imaginary topic may fit better next time. Observe this exchange rather than prove speed, intentions or tolerance.

title.zh: 分享停止或换话题的约定
title.en: Share an agreement about stopping or changing topics

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“打趣时，怎样一句话表示想停下或换回正事，会让你更容易说？”对方无需先证明自己开得起玩笑，也不必公开过去的经历。分享这份说明可以讨论互动方式，不授权截图围观、测试朋友底线或用均分解释别人的反应。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “During teasing, what short way to stop or return to the practical topic would feel easy to use?” No proof of tolerance or disclosure of past experiences is needed. Sharing this guide can open discussion without authorising screenshot audiences, tests of a friend’s limits or explanations of their reactions through your mean.
